MessageService

class MessageService(parent)[source]

Bases: object

Centralized service for displaying user messages.

Provides a clean, translatable and testable interface for showing information, warnings, errors and confirmation dialogs. Follows Qt’s QMessageBox signature: text first, title optional.

Parameters:
parentQWidget

Parent widget of the dialogs.

Attributes:
parentQWidget

The widget used as parent for all dialogs.

titlestr

Default dialog title: the window title of the top-level ancestor of parent, read when the service is created.

Methods

info(text, title=None)

Show an information message dialog.

warning(text, title=None)

Show a warning message dialog.

critical(text, title=None)

Show a critical error message dialog.

question(text, title=None, default_no=True)

Show a Yes/No question dialog with translated buttons.

critical_global(text, title=None)

Show a critical dialog when no parent widget is available.

Notes

The texts are shown as given, so callers pass already translated strings. Only the Yes/No button labels of question are translated here.

question(text, title=None, default_no=True)[source]

Display a Yes/No question dialog with translated buttons.

Parameters:
textstr

The question text to display.

titlestr | None, optional

Dialog title. Default is None, which uses title.

default_nobool, optional

If True, “No” is the default button; otherwise “Yes”. Default is True.

Returns:
bool

True if the user clicked “Yes”, False otherwise (including closing the dialog).

Notes

The button labels (pt_BR source texts “Sim” and “Não”) are translated at runtime with QCoreApplication.translate in the "MessageService" context, because the standard buttons do not take the context of the parent widget.

static critical_global(text, title=None)[source]

Show a critical dialog when no parent widget is available.

Parameters:
textstr

The error message to display.

titlestr | None, optional

Dialog title. Default is None, which uses AppConfig.get_title().

Notes

A temporary hidden QWidget, with the application icon, is created as parent of the modal dialog and scheduled for deletion afterwards. A QApplication must already exist.
